{{Quote|Whatever happened to the good ol' days of civil piracy, huh? Yarvok takes hostage. Yarvok gets paid. No one gets shot.|Yarvok|<ref name="Marauders" />}}
'''Yarvok''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]]<ref name="Marauders" /> and leader of the [[Nova Blades]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] gang living during the [[third Galactic War]].<ref name="Pets">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=codex|Invasive Species on Dantooine}}</ref> In [[3627 BBY]],<ref name="TOR Dates Forums">{{TOR updates|5.10.3}}</ref> the Nova Blades&mdash;who were led by Yarvok and paid by the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]&mdash;launched the [[Dantooine Incursion]].<ref name="Marauders" /> During the fighting, Yarvok went rogue and with his crew gained control of the [[Banir Regional Energy Complex|Dantooine Power Station]], requesting a ransom of fifteen million [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] be paid to his [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R0-B5U]] in exchange for its [[Reactor/Legends|reactor]].<ref name="RR" />

[[3626 BBY|By the next year]],<ref name="TOR Dates Pet">{{TOR updates|6.3}}. The relevant Codex entry was released with this update.</ref> Yarvok's beast wrangler [[Krupo]] lost many of Yarvok's prized pets when Krupo's ship crashed on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], angering Yarvok. Yarvok threatened to [[Death/Legends|kill]] Krupo if his missing pets were not located and returned to him at once, as Yarvok feared for their safety.<ref name="Pets" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|At last, someone who understands the civility of piracy! Why fight when you can just pay? That is the Yarvok way!|Yarvok, upon finally being paid the fifteen million credit ransom|<ref name="Marauders" />}}
Yarvok was first added to the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' as part of the digital expansion [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne|''Knights of the Eternal Throne'']] in the Dantooine Incursion. If the player pays Yarvok the fifteen million credits he demands he will leave peacefully, otherwise, the player will need to defeat him in battle to urge him to go.<ref name="RR" />
